platform_notes: Gap-fill round across the Valor and Dejavoo families. Valor terminals (Linux VL100 Pro/VL110/VP100/VL300 and the Android VL550/VP550E/VP550C/VP350/VP800), the RCKT reader and the Virtual Terminal all talk to Valor's own network (the 'switch'), whose response codes are now documented from Valor's current knowledge base (kb.valorpaytech.com) and Troubleshooting Q&A. Dejavoo P and QD Android terminals run the iPOSpays (DvPay) payment app; the iPOSpays portal/virtual terminal and the terminal software are described by Dejavoo's release notes, and two processor/POS-vendor guides add PIN pad pairing and SPIn bypass.

entries.title: Reprint a transaction receipt on the Android terminals (VL550 / VP550C / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Reprint Receipt.
entries.quote: VL500 / VL550 / VP500 / VP550 / VP550C / VP550E / VP800= Menu button, Reprint Receipt

entries.title: Key in a card by hand on the Android terminals (VL550 / VP550C / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Start the sale as usual.
At the Present Card screen, select the Manual Entry button to continue.
entries.quote: At the Present Card screen select the Manual Entry button to continue.

entries.title: Where Reset Terminal (soft reset) is on the Android terminals
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Settings.
Choose Utilities.
Choose Reset Terminal.
entries.quote: VL500 / VL550 / VP500 / VP550C / VP550E / VP800 = Menu Button > Settings > Utilities > Reset Terminal
entries.note: The FAQ gives only the menu path. Valor's soft reset article for the Linux models says a reset clears the terminal's database and needs the master password.

entries.title: Battery behaves inconsistently (VL110 / VL550 / VP550E)
steps: Let the battery run down to 0% until the terminal powers itself off.
Let it charge overnight.
Use the charging cable and wall adapter that came with the terminal.
entries.quote: Discharge the battery and let it charge overnight. Ensure you are using the provided charging cable and wall adapter to ensure the best use case.
entries.note: The current knowledge base lists VL110 / VL500 / VL550 / VP550E for this answer.

entries.title: Receipt prints very light (VL110 / VL550 / VP550E)
steps: Make sure the receipt tray is clean and closed properly.
On a VL110, make sure the terminal is not in Power Save mode.
Make sure the battery is at 45% or more.
entries.quote: ensure the Terminal is not in Power Save mode (VL110 only) and has at least 45% battery life.(VL110 / VL500 / VL550 / VP550E)

entries.title: Connection types supported: VL550 / VP550E / VP800
steps: These terminals connect by cellular or Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: VL500 / VL550 / VP500 / VP550E / VP800 = Cellular, WIFI

entries.title: Make the terminal use its SIM (cellular) connection: VL550 / VP550E / VP800
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Settings.
Choose WIFI Config.
Toggle Wi-Fi off.
entries.quote: VL500 / VL550 / VP500 / VP550E / VP800 = Menu Button, Settings, WIFI Config, toggle WIFI Off.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: dual pricing and BIN-based surcharge are supported
steps: Dual Pricing is available in the Virtual Terminal.
It detects whether the card is debit or credit (BIN detection).
entries.quote: Yes! Dual Pricing is available via the Virtual Terminal. This will allow BIN Detection when using Debit or Credit cards.
entries.note: Differs from the older Freshdesk copy of the FAQ, which said dual pricing was not available in the Virtual Terminal. This is Valor's current knowledge base.

entries.title: Update a VL300, VP300 or VP300 Pro PIN pad to the latest app version
steps: Make sure the PIN pad is connected properly to its terminal.
Run a Package Download so the latest software is installed.
If nothing updates, App Download has to be switched on for the terminal in the Online Portal first.
entries.quote: Ensure the device is connected appropriately to the VL100 / VP100 / VP300 Pro and perform a Package Download to ensure the latest software is installed.
entries.note: Valor says the ISO must toggle App Download to Enabled in the Online Portal for this to work.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Invalid Parameter
steps: Close the terminal's batch from the Online Portal.
Try the download again.
entries.quote: Close the Terminal’s batch via the Online Portal, then reattempt the Download.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: View a previous batch on a VL500-series terminal
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Report.
Choose Closed Batch or Detailed Report.
entries.quote: VL500 = Menu Button, Report, Closed Batch or Detailed Report
entries.note: The knowledge base names the VL500 for this path.

entries.title: Parameter Disabled (when reloading the EPI after a reset)
steps: This message appears when the terminal tries to reload its EPI and ParamDownload is not enabled for that EPI in the Online Portal.
ParamDownload has to be enabled on the Online Portal for that EPI, then the reload can be tried again.
entries.quote: it will communicate "Parameter Disabled" when attempting to reload the EPI

entries.title: Soft reset a VL100 / VL110 / VP100 (current knowledge base steps)
steps: Press the Menu button (three lines), then the Down Arrow, then Host Utility.
Enter the password (default is the last 4 digits of the EPI).
Press the Down Arrow, then Reset Terminal.
Enter the Valor master password 82567729 and press OK. This clears the database and resets the terminal.
ParamDownload must be enabled in the Online Portal for that EPI, or the terminal will say Parameter Disabled when it reloads.
entries.quote: Enter the **Valor Master Password (82567729)** followed by **OK button** to **Clear Database** and successfully **Reset the Terminal**.
entries.note: A reset clears the terminal's database; do it with support.

entries.title: VP800: connect a cash drawer
steps: Check that the cash drawer is compatible with the terminal.
You need the cash drawer, the terminal and the Multi-Comm Hub.
Connect the cash drawer with an RJ11/RJ12 cable to the Cash Drawer port on the Multi-Comm Hub.
Dock the VP800 on the Multi-Comm Hub.
entries.quote: Connect the cash drawer via **RJ11/RJ12 Cable** to the **Cash Drawer** port on the **Multi-Comm Hub**.

entries.title: VP800: turn on the cash drawer in the terminal settings
steps: On the terminal go to Settings, then Utility, then Cash Draw.
Enable the cash drawer.
Set the payment type and transaction status that should open it.
entries.quote: Enable the cash drawer and set payment type and transaction status.

entries.title: VP800: open the cash drawer by hand
steps: Go to the terminal's settings.
Select the CASH DRAW OPEN option.
entries.quote: the cash drawer can be manually opened by navigating to the settings and selecting the "**CASH DRAW OPEN**" option

entries.title: Portal setting: Server/Clerk Setup (also turns on tip adjust)
steps: Server/Clerk Setup makes the terminal ask for a clerk or server ID during transactions.
Turning it on also activates tip adjustment.
entries.quote: Server/Clerk Setup – Enables clerk/server ID entry during transactions for tracking; also activates tip adjustment functionality.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Clerk Mandate (clerk ID asked on every sale)
steps: When Server/Clerk Setup is on, Clerk Mandate makes the clerk or server ID required on every transaction.
entries.quote: Clerk Mandate – Requires clerk/server ID entry on every transaction when Server/Clerk Setup is enabled.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: tip suggestions on screen and on the receipt
steps: Smart Tip prints four suggested tip options on the receipt.
Tip On Screen shows the Smart Tip suggestions on the terminal for the customer to choose.
Tip On Receipt prints a tip line so the customer can write in a tip.
Show "No Tip" Option adds a No Tip button.
entries.quote: Tip On Screen – Displays Smart Tip suggestions directly on the payment terminal for customer selection.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Max Tip
steps: Max Tip sets the largest tip, as a percentage or dollar amount, that the terminal will accept.
entries.quote: Max Tip – Sets the maximum tip percentage or dollar amount to prevent excessive tipping.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Fixed Tip (a tip is added to every sale)
steps: Fixed Tip automatically applies a preset tip percentage or dollar amount to all transactions.
entries.quote: Fixed Tip – Automatically applies a preset tip percentage or dollar amount to all transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Receipt for Tip Adjust
steps: When this is on, the terminal prints a new receipt each time a tip is adjusted.
entries.quote: Receipt for Tip Adjust – Prints a new receipt whenever a tip adjustment is made after the initial transaction.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Receipt for Declined Transactions
steps: When this is on, the terminal prints a receipt for declined or failed transactions.
entries.quote: Receipt for Declined Transactions – Prints receipts for declined or failed transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: "No Transactions to Settle" slip at settlement
steps: The No Transaction Report setting makes the terminal print a slip saying "No Transactions to Settle" when the batch is empty.
entries.quote: No Transaction Report – Prints a slip stating “No Transactions to Settle” if no transactions exist.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Email Report (batch report by email)
steps: Email Report sends the batch settlement report to the primary merchant account email on file.
entries.quote: Email Report – Emails the batch settlement report to the primary merchant account email on file.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: which report prints at settlement
steps: Detailed Report prints a detailed list of transactions at batch settlement.
Summary Report prints a summarized version.
Settlement Report Tip adds tip information to the settlement report.
entries.quote: Detailed Report – Prints a detailed list of transactions during batch settlement.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Hide Receipt Option
steps: Hide Receipt Option turns off SMS receipts and the SMS collection screens.
It overrides the SMS Receipt and Paper Receipt settings.
entries.quote: Hide Receipt Option – Disables SMS receipts and SMS collection screens for Engage my Customer; overrides SMS and Paper receipt settings.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: SMS Receipt (merchant copy must be reprinted)
steps: SMS Receipt sends the receipt by text message.
If a merchant copy is needed it has to be reprinted.
entries.quote: SMS Receipt – Sends a receipt via SMS; merchant copy must be reprinted if required.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: signature line and merchant receipt copy (not on RCKT, VP550E or Virtual Terminal)
steps: Force On Screen Signature asks for a signature on the screen for signature debit or credit sales.
Forced Signature prints a signature line on paper receipts.
Forced Signature and Merchant Receipt Option are not supported on the RCKT, VP550E or Virtual Terminal.
entries.quote: Forced Signature – Prints a signature line on paper receipts (unsupported on RCKT, VP550E, Virtual Terminal).
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Sleep Mode / Timer
steps: Sleep Mode / Timer sets how long the terminal sits idle before it goes into power-save mode.
entries.quote: Sleep Mode / Timer – Defines how long the terminal remains idle before entering power-save mode.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Terminal shuts down by itself at a set time (Auto Shutdown setting)
steps: Auto Shutdown is a portal setting that schedules the terminal to shut down at a set time.
entries.quote: Auto Shutdown – Schedules the terminal to shut down at a set time.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Batch Out (manual or automatic)
steps: Batch Out chooses manual or automatic batch settlement.
In automatic mode a specific time can be set.
entries.quote: Batch Out – Chooses between manual and automatic batch settlement; automatic mode allows setting a specific time.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: VP800: what the customer-facing screen shows
steps: A portal setting chooses whether the customer-facing display shows the current time or an image.
entries.quote: Display on Customer Facing Screen – Displays either the current time or an image on customer-facing displays (VP800 only).
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Split Payment
steps: Split Payment lets one transaction be split into up to five payment methods.
entries.quote: Split Payment – Enables splitting a transaction into up to five payment methods.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Cash Back on Debit
steps: Cash Back on Debit lets customers get cash back on PIN-verified debit transactions.
entries.quote: Cash Back on Debit – Allows customers to receive cash back on PIN-verified debit transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Change Management on Cash Transactions
steps: With this on, the merchant enters the cash received and the terminal works out the change.
entries.quote: Change Management on Cash Transactions – Lets merchants enter the cash received to calculate the correct change automatically.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Disable All Passwords
steps: Disable All Passwords turns off the terminal-level passwords.
The master password is still needed for resets and key actions.
entries.quote: Disable All Passwords – Disables terminal-level passwords, while still requiring the master password for resets and key actions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Portal settings: password prompts for refund, EBT, void and pre-auth
steps: Password for Refund adds a password requirement for refunds.
Prompt Password For: EBT, VOID, PreAUTH makes the terminal ask for a password on those transaction types.
entries.quote: Prompt Password For: EBT, VOID, PreAUTH – Enforces password prompts when performing these transaction types.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: No signature or receipt on small sales (QSR setting)
steps: QSR (Quick Serve Restaurant) skips the signature and receipt printing below a set dollar amount.
entries.quote: QSR (Quick Serve Restaurant) – Bypasses signature and receipt printing below a defined dollar threshold.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: manual card entry on credit and debit
steps: Manual Entry on Credit allows credit card numbers to be keyed in.
Manual Entry on Debit allows debit card numbers to be keyed in and needs credit manual entry enabled.
Bypass CVV Entry skips the CVV on manual entries and also needs credit manual entry enabled.
entries.quote: Manual Entry on Debit – Allows manual entry of debit card numbers (requires credit manual entry enabled).
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Present Card Prompt
steps: Present Card Prompt asks whether the card is present when card details are keyed in by hand.
entries.quote: Present Card Prompt – Asks customers to confirm card presence when entering details manually.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Gift Card Partial Approval
steps: Gift Card Partial Approval allows a split payment when the gift card balance does not cover the sale.
entries.quote: Gift Card Partial Approval – Supports split-pay when gift card balance is insufficient.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: AVS (address or ZIP asked during a sale)
steps: AVS makes the terminal require the address, the ZIP, or both for verification during transactions.
entries.quote: AVS – Requires address, ZIP, or both for verification during transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: tax on sales
steps: State Tax applies a set tax percentage to transactions.
Include Tax for Cash charges tax on cash transactions as well.
Show Remove Tax gives an option to remove tax at the amount confirmation screen; it needs the differential removal options enabled too.
entries.quote: Show Remove Tax – Gives the option to remove tax at the amount confirmation screen. Requires differential removal options to also be enabled.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Access Valor Store (Android only)
steps: Access Valor Store gives the terminal access to the Valor Store marketplace.
It is for Android devices only and has a limited set of apps.
entries.quote: Access Valor Store – Grants access to Valor Store marketplace (Android devices only, limited apps).
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: receipt header and footer lines
steps: Line 1 shows the store name.
Lines 2 to 4 default to the store's primary address, secondary address and phone number and can be customized.
Line 5 is empty by default.
A footer message prints beneath the disclaimer; more footer lines can be added with +Add.
entries.quote: Footer – Prints a short message beneath the disclaimer on receipts. Additional footer lines can be added using “+Add.”
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Which transaction types a Valor terminal can show (POS Menu Configuration)
steps: Default / Credit covers Sale, Void, Pre-Auth, Ticket, Refund, Pre-Sale and Post-Auth.
Default / Debit covers Sale, Pre-Auth and Ticket.
EBT Food covers Sale, Refund, Balance Inquiry and Withdrawal.
EBT Cash covers Balance Inquiry and Withdrawal.
Cash covers Sale and Refund.
Gift Card covers Balance Inquiry, Add Value, Activate, Sale and Refund.
entries.quote: DEFAULT / DEBIT – Allows debit card processing with Sale, Pre-Auth, and Ticket options.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Deferred Auth (offline transactions): turn it on for a terminal in the portal
steps: Log in to the Online Portal.
Go to Device Management.
Find the EPI, select the vertical ellipsis, then Edit Parameters.
Select the Terminal & Transaction tab, then the Transaction sub-tab.
Toggle Offline Transactions to Enabled.
Set the offline transaction limits and settings.
Select SAVE.
entries.quote: Toggle Offline Transactions to Enabled.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Deferred Auth: switch the terminal to offline mode (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-middle of the screen.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select Enable Offline Mode and accept the terms by pressing YES.
An Offline icon at the top of the screen shows the terminal is in offline mode.
entries.quote: Select Utility followed by Deferred AUTH.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: print the offline transaction report (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select Offline Reports.
Select Open Summary or Detailed Report to print.
entries.quote: Select either Open Summary or Detailed Report to Print Report.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: upload offline transactions (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select Upload Offline Txn to capture the transactions.
entries.quote: Select Upload Offline Txn to Capture Transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: review pending offline transactions (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select View Transaction.
entries.quote: Select View Transaction to Capture Transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: switch the terminal to offline mode (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Offline Disabled and accept the terms by pressing YES.
"Offline" at the top-left of the screen shows the terminal is in offline mode.
entries.quote: Select Offline Disabled followed by accepting the terms by pressing YES.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: upload offline transactions (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Upload Transaction to capture the transactions.
entries.quote: Select Upload Transaction to Capture Transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: review pending offline transactions (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select View Transaction.
entries.quote: Select View Transaction to Review Transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: print the offline transaction report (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Report.
Select Detailed Report or Summary to print.
entries.quote: Select either Detailed Report or Summary to Print Report.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: leave offline mode (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Offline Enabled and confirm with YES.
Any transactions not yet uploaded will now upload and be captured.
entries.quote: Any Transactions not Uploaded will now Upload and be Captured.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: taking cards when the network is unstable
steps: Deferred authorization lets the terminal process transactions locally when the network is unstable.
The "Enable Offline transactions" flag has to be enabled in the Valor Portal first.
It can be used for sale and refund transactions.
Once a stable connection is back, the transactions are uploaded.
entries.quote: Deferred authorization can be implemented for sale and refund transaction types.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Deferred Auth: limits on offline transactions
steps: The maximum amount for a single offline transaction is 500 dollars.
The maximum total before a batch out is 5000 dollars.
The maximum number of offline transactions per day is 60.
The maximum number of offline transactions for a single card is 5.
The merchant sets the actual limits in the Valor Portal within these maximums.
entries.quote: The maximum number of transactions for a single card
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Deferred Auth: delete (void) an offline transaction on the terminal
steps: The "Delete Offline transaction" portal option lets the merchant delete individual offline transactions on the terminal.
With the Prompt option, the terminal asks "Do you want to delete this transaction?".
With the password protected option, the merchant enters the last four digits of the EPI number.
entries.quote: When the merchant chooses the Prompt option, the merchant can delete the transaction after providing the
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Deferred Auth: when offline transactions are uploaded
steps: The portal's "Transaction upload mode" has two options: Upload before batch out, and manual upload.
entries.quote: transactions through two options – Upload before batch out and manual upload

entries.title: Deferred Auth on the Linux terminals: turn on offline mode from the offline icon
steps: After the terminal has been updated with the new parameters, a small offline icon appears in the top-right corner of the screen.
Select the icon to reach "Enable Offline Mode".
Select Yes to agree to the terms and conditions.
Another way: go to the main menu settings, select Utility, enter the EPI password, choose Deferred Auth, then Enable Offline Mode and Yes.
entries.quote: After updating the POS terminal with the necessary parameters, a small offline icon will appear in the
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Deferred Auth: upload and settle offline transactions (manual upload mode)
steps: Connect the terminal to a stable internet connection.
Select the offline icon or button to open the offline menu.
Select "Upload Offline Transaction" to upload all offline transactions.
Go to the main menu and select Settlement.
Enter the password or passcode for the EPI to batch out the uploaded transactions.
entries.quote: "Upload Offline Transaction" to upload all offline transactions.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Deferred Auth: settle offline transactions (Upload Before Batch Out mode)
steps: Go to the main menu and select Settlement.
A pop-up shows the EPI ID; enter its password or passcode.
Once confirmed, the offline transactions are credited to the merchant's account.
entries.quote: This process applies when the “Upload Before Batch Out” mode is enabled in the Valor Portal.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: VL550: run a fleet card (fuel) transaction
steps: Tap the Fuel icon on the terminal and choose the fuel type.
If needed, tap Service or Store and choose the service or product, or type the product code in the search bar.
Enter the transaction details and check the summary.
Complete the vehicle verification (odometer reading, Vehicle ID, driver number, user ID).
Process the payment.
entries.quote: To initiate a fleet card transaction, the user taps the "Fuel" icon on the POS terminal.

steps: Log in to the Valor Portal.
Go to Settings, then Fleet.
Organize products under Products, Product Types and Product Categories.
To change a product, select the vertical ellipses and Edit.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: run an ACH sale
steps: In the Virtual Terminal, select the ACH sale sub tag under the ACH tag.
Fill in the transaction details with a valid account and routing number.
Select Debit or Credit as the TXN Type.
Select PROCESS PAYMENT.
A pop-up shows the status of the transaction.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: set up a recurring ACH payment
steps: In the Virtual Terminal, select the ACH Recurring sub tag under the ACH tag.
Fill in the frequency and other details with a valid account and routing number.
Select PROCESS PAYMENT.
A pop-up shows the status of the recurring transaction.
entries.quote: Select ACH Recurring sub tag, Under ACH tag visible in the Virtual Terminal.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: see the ACH threshold
steps: Go to Setting in the sidebar menu.
Go to the ACH Threshold tab.
entries.quote: Navigate to ACH Threshold tab.
entries.note: Per Valor's ACH guide the ISO sets the threshold; the merchant can view it.

entries.title: Portal: view or delete an ACH transaction
steps: ACH transactions have their own tabs in the transaction module.
From the vertical ellipses of a transaction the merchant can delete it or see an overview.

entries.title: ValorPay app: run a refund
steps: Select the Down Arrow box next to Sale on the home screen.
Select Refund.
Enter the amount, then Process Payment.

entries.title: Dejavoo terminal paired to a POS is not connecting, freezing or not processing payments
steps: Confirm the terminal has power and is securely connected to its dock or charging cable.
If you use Wi-Fi, confirm you are on the correct network.
Turn the terminal off.
Wait 10 seconds.
Turn the terminal back on and wait for it to start up fully.
Confirm the terminal is paired or connected in the POS app.
Try a known-good network if one is available.
entries.quote: Confirm the terminal has power and is securely connected to its dock or charging cable.
entries.note: POS vendor guide for Dejavoo terminals driven by a POS over SPIn; steps about the vendor's own iPad app are left out.

entries.title: POS cannot start a payment: take the card on the terminal in Bypass mode
steps: Use Bypass mode only when the POS app gets connection errors and cannot start a payment, while the terminal and internet still work.
On the terminal screen, tap the Bypass button in the top-right corner.
Enter the amount to charge on the terminal.
Have the customer tap, insert or swipe the card as normal.
Keep the terminal receipt.
When the POS works again, exit Bypass mode and run a normal test transaction from the POS.
entries.quote: On the terminal screen, tap the Bypass button in the top-right corner.
entries.note: POS vendor guide for Dejavoo terminals driven by a POS over SPIn; steps about the vendor's own iPad app are left out.

entries.title: Bypass button does nothing (Restricted Bypass mode)
steps: If tapping the Bypass button does nothing, Restricted Bypass mode is on and the terminal needs a PIN first.
Tap and hold the Dejavoo SPIn logo in the center of the screen for 2 to 3 seconds.
Enter the 4-digit PIN provided by your manager.
At "Please select an access mode." select Full Access and press OK.
Tap the Bypass button in the top-right corner.
entries.quote: Tap and hold the Dejavoo SPIn logo in the center of the screen for 2 to 3 seconds.
entries.note: POS vendor guide for Dejavoo terminals driven by a POS over SPIn; steps about the vendor's own iPad app are left out.

entries.title: Bypass mode sales do not appear in the POS
steps: Transactions run in Bypass mode are processed on their own and are not recorded in the POS.
Once the POS works again, ring up the same items in the POS.
Choose Cash or a custom payment method instead of card; the card was already charged on the terminal, so do not run it again.
Repeat for each Bypass mode transaction.
entries.quote: The card was already charged on the terminal, so do not run it again.
entries.note: POS vendor guide for Dejavoo terminals driven by a POS over SPIn; steps about the vendor's own iPad app are left out.

entries.title: Key-driven Bypass steps (F1 > SPIN Bypass) from the Material POS guide
steps: Press F1.
Use the down arrow to select "SPIN Bypass".
Press OK.
Enter password 1234 and press OK.
Key in the amount to charge and press OK.
Have the customer complete the transaction as normal.
entries.quote: Use the down arrow to select “SPIN Bypass”
entries.note: The page shows two headings (P-series devices, Z8 devices) followed by one list of steps and does not say which heading the steps belong to; filed under the Z8 only. Password 1234 is the vendor's stated value.

entries.title: What happens to sales taken in bypass mode during a gateway outage
steps: Transactions processed in bypass mode are batched and submitted once the gateway is back online.
Once the outage is over, run a test transaction to confirm everything works normally.
entries.quote: Transactions processed in bypass mode will be batched and submitted once the gateway is back online.
entries.note: POS vendor guide for Dejavoo terminals driven by a POS over SPIn; steps about the vendor's own iPad app are left out.

entries.title: P-series terminals can take sales with no network (Offline Mode)
steps: Offline Mode lets Dejavoo gateway-powered P-series terminals process sale transactions without a network connection.
entries.quote: Offline Mode allows merchants using Dejavoo gateway-powered P-series terminals to process sale transactions without a network connection.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Offline Mode: limit of 150 offline transactions
steps: The offline transaction threshold was raised from 30 to 150.
entries.quote: Raised the offline transaction threshold from 30 to 150.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Firmware upgrades install automatically after a parameter update
steps: Firmware upgrades are applied automatically after parameter updates.
entries.quote: Firmware upgrades are now applied automatically after parameter updates.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Upgrade the terminal firmware by hand from the DVStore app
steps: Open the DVStore app on the terminal and upgrade the firmware from there.
The terminal also runs an automatic upgrade every 24 hours.
entries.quote: Merchants can now manually upgrade the firmware on their payment terminal from the DVStore app, in addition to the automatic upgrade that runs every 24 hours.
entries.note: The release note gives no menu steps. A later note says DvStore downloads over mobile/SIM data are available on supported Dejavoo P and QD devices.

entries.title: Changing the TPN on a terminal needs a one-time passcode

entries.quote: A one-time passcode (OTP) is now required to change the Terminal Profile Number (TPN) on a POS terminal.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Card Removed by User

entries.quote: even when the transaction had already been successfully approved by the processor
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: P3: "Invalid Amount" on a ticket with tip after a pre-auth
steps: This was a software issue on P3 terminals that Dejavoo has fixed: approved pre-auths followed by tickets that include a tip now process as expected.
entries.quote: Approved pre-auths followed by tip-inclusive tickets now process as expected on P3 terminals, without returning an "Invalid Amount" error.
entries.note: If a P3 still shows this, its software may be out of date.

entries.title: P3: status check runs right after the network reconnects
steps: P3 terminals now run their status checks automatically as soon as the network reconnects.
entries.quote: P3 terminals now automatically perform status checks immediately after network reconnection.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: P1: transaction threshold limit issue that needed a reboot (fixed in build 10089)
steps: Dejavoo fixed a transaction threshold limit issue on the P1, so a reboot is no longer needed.
entries.quote: Fixes the transaction threshold limit issue, eliminating the need to reboot.
entries.note: If a P1 still needs rebooting for this, its software may be out of date.

entries.title: P12: the amount screen dims after 30 seconds
steps: On the P12, the Amount Entry screen dims after 30 seconds of inactivity to save battery. This is normal.
entries.quote: On P12 devices, the Amount Entry screen now dims after 30 seconds of inactivity to save battery.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: P18: Register Lite, Device Alerts and P17 PIN pad over USB hub
steps: The P18 supports Command and Communication Center, Register Lite and Device Alerts.
It also supports PIN pad integration with the Dejavoo P17 through a USB hub.
entries.quote: The Dejavoo P18 payment terminal now supports Command and Communication Center, Register Lite, Device Alerts, and PIN pad integration with the Dejavoo P17 via USB hub.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: FEE N/A PROFILE
steps: Dejavoo fixed an issue where this error appeared on the first transaction after a terminal reboot when deep linking was used with a fee profile.
entries.quote: Fixed an issue where the error appeared on the first transaction after a terminal reboot.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: "Spring framework" error during an incremental auth
steps: Dejavoo fixed an issue where a Spring Framework error appeared on the terminal during incremental auth.
entries.quote: Resolves an issue where a Spring Framework error would appear on the merchant's Dejavoo payment terminal.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Transaction data not found (looking up a pre-auth after settlement)
steps: Dejavoo fixed this error so pre-auth transactions can be retrieved after batch settlement.
entries.quote: Fixes the 'Transaction data not found' error, allowing successful retrieval of Pre Auth transactions after batch settlement.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Service is Busy (POS-driven terminal, after batch settlement)
steps: Dejavoo changed the software so that during SPIn transactions the POS no longer shows 'Service is Busy' after batch settlement.
entries.quote: During SPIn transactions, the POS no longer displays 'Service is Busy' after batch settlement.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Show/Settle Batch: transactions missing after entering the password (fixed)
steps: Dejavoo fixed a batch error on standalone terminals: transactions now appear correctly after the password is entered for Show/Settle Batch.
entries.quote: Transactions now appear correctly after password entry for Show/Settle Batch.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Restricted Mode: a POS-driven PIN pad cannot open the menu or SPIn Bypass
steps: Restricted Mode keeps an integrated PIN pad in listening mode so the menu and SPIn Bypass cannot be reached.
entries.quote: Ensures the integrated PIN pad device remains in listening mode to prevent access to the menu and SPIn Bypass.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: PIN cannot be bypassed on tapped (contactless) cards
steps: PIN Bypass is not supported for contactless card transactions (a Mastercard requirement).
entries.quote: PIN Bypass not supported for contactless card transactions.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Debit cashback amount is rejected and reset to $0.00
steps: A maximum cashback limit can be set for debit transactions.
Cashback amounts above the limit are rejected and reset to $0.00.
entries.quote: Cashback amounts above the limit are rejected and reset to $0.00.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Customer copy print prompt and timer
steps: The Customer Copy Print Confirmation prompt can be turned on or off.
A customer copy print timer can be set between 3 and 30 seconds.
entries.quote: set a customer copy print timer between 3 and 30 seconds
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: ZIP / postal code formats accepted for keyed cards
steps: Manual entry on the terminal accepts 5-, 6- and 9-character alphanumeric ZIP or postal codes.
entries.quote: POS manual entry now accepts 5-, 6-, and 9-character alphanumeric ZIP/postal code formats.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Batch settlement receipt can be sorted by transaction or card type
steps: Batch receipts can be sorted by transaction or card type on Dejavoo terminals.
entries.quote: Merchants can now sort batch receipts by transaction or card type on Dejavoo terminals.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Settle By Store: settle several terminals of one store at once
steps: Merchants with multiple TPNs under one store can settle the batches for all TPNs at once, or pick specific ones.
entries.quote: Settle By Store enables merchants with multiple TPNs under a single store to settle batches instantly.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Tip Adjust by Store: adjust tips for other terminals in the same store
steps: Tips can be adjusted for multiple TPNs from a single device or batch, as long as they are in the same store.
entries.quote: Merchants using POS or CloudPOS terminals can adjust the tip for multiple TPNs from a single device or batch within the same store.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: See untipped and server reports of other terminals in the same store
steps: Untipped and server reports of other TPNs in the same store can be viewed from a single terminal.
entries.quote: View untipped and server reports of other TPNs within the same store from a single terminal.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Incremental Auth: raise the amount of a pre-auth
steps: On gateway-powered terminals, Incremental Auth increases the amount first authorized in a pre-auth.
entries.quote: Merchants using Gateway-powered terminals can utilize Incremental Auth to increase the amount initially authorized in a Pre-Auth.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Checks can be logged as a payment type on the terminal
steps: Checks can be logged as a payment type directly on the terminal.
entries.quote: Merchants can now log checks as a valid payment type directly on their POS terminals.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: EBT chip (EMV) is on by default for new terminals
steps: New POS TPNs have EBT EMV enabled by default.
entries.quote: New POS TPNs now have EBT EMV enabled by default
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Last Few Batches filter for viewing batches on the terminal
steps: A "Last Few Batches" filter makes it easier to view batches on gateway-powered terminals.
entries.quote: New filter to make it easier to view batches on Dejavoo Gateway Powered terminals and iPOSgo!
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: QD series: Mini Receipt
steps: A Mini Receipt option is available for gateway-powered QD devices.
entries.quote: Mini Receipt for Gateway-powered QD devices.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Receipt header can have 6 lines
steps: The receipt header allows 2 additional lines, for a total of 6.
entries.quote: Allows 2 additional lines, for a total of 6 header lines on the receipt.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Server Report: look up transactions by server ID
steps: The Server Report retrieves transactions using the server ID.
entries.quote: Effortlessly retrieve transactions using the server ID.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: Sale interrupted by a network drop: status shown if the network returns within 5 minutes
steps: If the network reconnects within 5 minutes, the transaction's status is displayed and approved transactions are no longer voided.
The status can be checked in the Send E-Receipt section.
entries.quote: Transactions will now display their status if the network reconnects within 5 minutes, with approved transactions no longer voided, and can be checked in the new Send E-Receipt section.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; describes how current terminal software behaves.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal password must be at least 12 characters
steps: The minimum length of the iPOSpays login password is 12 characters (raised from 10).
entries.quote: We have updated the iPOSpays login password minimum requirement from 10 to 12 characters.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal: password has expired
steps: Complete the MFA verification.
From the expiry pop-up go directly to the Reset Password page; no reset link by email is needed.
entries.quote: Users with an expired password can now go directly to the Reset Password page from the expiry pop-up after completing MFA verification, without requesting a reset link by email.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal: "Invalid password" when resetting the password
steps: The password reset box now gives specific feedback on what is wrong with the entry instead of a generic "Invalid password" message.
entries.quote: the message on the password reset box on the iPOSpays portal will now provide specific feedback based on the user’s input
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal: password reset link did not open the reset page (fixed)
steps: Dejavoo fixed the reset link so it opens the reset page even if other portal tabs are open.
entries.quote: This fix ensures the password reset link now properly directs to the reset page, even if other portal tabs are open.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal asks for a one-time code at login
steps: iPOSpays requires one-time codes for login (multi-factor authentication).
entries.quote: iPOSpays now requires one-time codes for login
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays login page shows a Terms and Conditions agreement
steps: A Terms and Conditions agreement is part of the iPOSpays login page.
entries.quote: a new Terms and Conditions agreement has been implemented on the iPOSpays login page
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: manual refunds ask for a security code (MFA)
steps: Manual refunds require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for each new session.
entries.quote: To enhance security, manual refunds will now require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for each new session.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: 6-digit security code when creating or editing a user
steps: A 6-digit security code must be entered to finish creating a user and when editing an existing user.
entries.quote: users will be required to enter a 6-digit security code to complete the user creation process and when editing an existing user
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: admins get an email when a new user is created
steps: iPOSpays Admin users get an automatic email when a new user is created under their account, by a primary or an add-on user.
entries.quote: Automatic email notification sent to iPOSpays Admin users when a new user is created under their account either by a primary or an add-on user.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: a user cannot see the Dashboard
steps: Access to the iPOSpays Dashboard is a privilege that ISOs and merchant admins turn on or off when creating users.
entries.quote: ISOs and Merchant admins can now control access to the iPOSpays Dashboard by enabling or disabling it as a privilege when creating new users.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays CloudPOS: a new user cannot issue refunds for the first 48 hours
steps: Newly created CloudPOS users can be restricted from issuing manual refunds during their first 48 hours.
This restriction is off by default and is enabled on request.
entries.quote: Newly created CloudPOS users can be restricted from issuing manual refunds during their first 48 hours.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: refunds on transactions older than 90 days
steps: Refunds can be processed for transactions older than 90 days.
entries.quote: Merchants can now process refunds for transactions older than 90 days.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: up to three refunds on one sale
steps: Up to three refunds can be issued for a single sale, as long as the total refunded does not exceed the original sale amount.
entries.quote: iPOSpays users can now issue up to three refunds for a single sale transaction, as long as the total refunded does not exceed the original sale amount.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: void or refund without entering an amount is a full void or refund
steps: A void or refund submitted without an amount is processed for the original transaction amount, as a full void or full refund.
entries.quote: with the original transaction amount automatically processed as a full Void or full Refund
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays CloudPOS: cash refunds
steps: Cash refunds can be processed on the CloudPOS Pay Now screen.
entries.quote: Merchants can now process cash refunds on the CloudPOS
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays CloudPOS: bank (ACH) refund without an original transaction
steps: Bank (ACH) refunds can be issued from CloudPOS without an original transaction.
entries.quote: Merchants can now issue Bank (ACH) refunds without an original transaction
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: an approved sale was voided automatically (wrong CVV or ZIP)
steps: The iPOS S.A.F.E Card Validation risk rule checks for an incorrect CVV and/or ZIP code.
If a transaction is approved but fails either check, it is voided automatically and the funds are released back to the customer's account.
entries.quote: If a transaction is approved but fails either check, it will be automatically voided, and the funds will be released back to the customer’s account.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: card-not-present sale declined for an address mismatch (Street Check)
steps: The Card Validation risk rule has a Street Check option that matches the street address (AVS).
When it is enabled, mismatched addresses trigger declines.
entries.quote: When enabled, mismatched addresses trigger declines
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: settlement report by email
steps: Merchants can get a consolidated settlement report by email, either right after each batch or as a daily summary.
It covers all TPNs under each store.
entries.quote: Merchants can now automatically receive a consolidated settlement report by email
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: settlement report email includes an Excel file
steps: Settlement report emails include an Excel attachment alongside the PDF.
entries.quote: Settlement report emails now include an Excel attachment alongside the PDF, applicable to POS, CloudPOS, and iPOSgo! apps.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: batch report contents
steps: Batch reports include a Transaction Summary with a breakdown of each transaction from each store.
Batch settlement reports include Card Brand, Subtotal and Fee details.

entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays Transaction Report: negative amounts and Settlement Status
steps: The Transaction Report shows refunds and voids with a negative sign.
It has a Settlement Status column.

entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays CloudPOS: settle a batch that has no card transactions
steps: CloudPOS merchants can settle batches even when there are no card transactions.
entries.quote: CloudPOS merchants can now settle batches even in the absence of any card transactions.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays My Customers: error when deleting a card
steps: An error message appears when a user tries to delete a card in My Customers that has a recurring payment linked to it.

entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.

entries.title: iPOSpays: what time recurring payments are charged
steps: Recurring payments are processed at 3:15 AM EST.

entries.note: From Dejavoo's iPOSpays release notes; no step-by-step portal guide is published.
